objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains preprocessor feature macros. There are therefore no custom data types to document.

Enumeration of scalar data types used within the Draco library, covering signed/unsigned integers of various widths, floating-point types, a boolean type, an invalid sentinel, and a count sentinel. DT_INVALID indicates an unset/unknown type; DT_TYPES_COUNT provides the number of defined types. Intended for runtime type tagging and size/behavior queries in Draco code.

A lightweight result type used to represent success or a specific error when returning from functions. It holds an error code and optional human-readable message. Methods allow checking success (ok), retrieving the code and message, and producing string forms. Copyable and movable. No dynamic ownership semantics beyond standard string storage.
Enumeration of Status result codes indicating success or specific error categories. Nested inside draco::Status.

Public decoder utility that wraps an external byte buffer and provides typed and bit-level decoding for Draco bitstreams. No ownership of the data is taken; callers must keep the underlying memory valid for the decoder's lifetime. Supports starting and ending a bit-decoding mode for LSB-first bit access, along with byte-aligned Decode/Peek operations, position control, and bitstream version tagging.

A growable encoding buffer that supports two modes: byte-aligned appends of arbitrary data and variable-length bit encoding. Provides APIs to start/end bit-encoding regions, push least-significant bits, and append raw bytes or typed values when not in bit mode. Exposes read-only data(), size(), and access to the underlying std::vector<char>. Construction/destruction are standard; internal ownership includes a unique_ptr to a nested BitEncoder used only during bit-encoding. Details of StartBitEncoding/EndBitEncoding behavior and buffer reservation are defined in the corresponding .cc file and are not visible here.

A concrete decoder class in namespace draco responsible for decoding Draco-compressed point clouds and meshes from a DecoderBuffer. Provides static inspection of encoded geometry type, methods to decode into new PointCloud/Mesh instances, and methods to decode into existing geometry objects. Exposes DecoderOptions via options() and allows skipping attribute transforms for specific attribute types. Construction details are not specified here; default constructor and destructor are implicitly declared. Ownership: holds a DecoderOptions member that it manages internally.

High-level helper class that configures and performs Draco geometry encoding. It derives from EncoderBase<EncoderOptionsBase<GeometryAttribute::Type>> and exposes convenience APIs to set speed, quantization, explicit quantization, prediction schemes, and encoding method, and to encode PointClouds and Meshes into an EncoderBuffer. Construction and destruction details are not shown here; only the interface is defined in this header.

Owns a collection of n-dimensional points and their associated PointAttribute objects (positions, colors, etc.), plus optional GeometryMetadata. Provides APIs to add/query attributes, manage metadata, deduplicate attributes/points (when enabled), compute a BoundingBox, and configure compression when DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED. Lifetime: users create, add attributes, set num_points, and optionally attach metadata. Destruction cleans up owned attributes and metadata.

Stateless functor that computes a content-based hash of a draco::PointCloud by combining point count, named-attribute indices, attribute payloads, and metadata. Intended for use in unordered containers or cache keys. Performance may be slow for large clouds.

functions.name: draco::DataTypeLength
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a single value of the given draco::DataType. Typical mapping matches the type suffix (e.g., DT_INT8/DT_UINT8 -> 1, DT_INT16/DT_UINT16 -> 2, DT_INT32/DT_UINT32/DT_FLOAT32 -> 4, DT_INT64/DT_UINT64/DT_FLOAT64 -> 8, DT_BOOL -> 1). Intended for callers that need to compute buffer sizes or element strides based on a Draco data type. Behavior for DT_INVALID or out-of-range enum values is not documented in this header and may be undefined/implementation-defined.
requirements: dt must be a valid draco::DataType enumerator corresponding to a concrete data size (i.e., not DT_INVALID and not DT_TYPES_COUNT).
Callers should not assume a nonzero return for invalid or unsupported values; behavior for such inputs is unspecified in this header.
The function is pure (no side effects) and can be called at any time; no initialization requirements are indicated.

functions.name: draco::IsDataTypeIntegral
functions.description: Returns true if the provided draco::DataType is an integral type; per the header comment, this includes all signed and unsigned integer types as well as DT_BOOL. Returns false for non-integer types (e.g., DT_FLOAT32, DT_FLOAT64). Useful when branching behavior based on whether the underlying type is integral.
requirements: dt should be a valid draco::DataType enumerator. Behavior for DT_INVALID or out-of-range values is not specified in this header.
Interprets DT_BOOL as integral per the documented comment.

functions.name: draco::Status::code
functions.description: Returns the current status code of this Status object. Use to test the outcome of an operation programmatically.
requirements: The Status instance must be a valid, initialized object.
No additional preconditions; callable at any time.

functions.name: draco::Status::error_msg_string
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the internal error message string associated with this Status. Useful for retrieving a full message without copying.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the Status object remains alive and its internal message is not modified.
The caller must not attempt to modify the returned string (it is const).

functions.name: draco::Status::error_msg
functions.description: Returns a C-string pointer to the internal error message. Convenience wrapper around error_msg_string().c_str().
requirements: The returned pointer is valid only while the referenced Status object remains alive and unchanged (any modification to the internal string may invalidate the pointer).
The returned pointer may be an empty string if no error message is set; it is never null.

functions.name: draco::Status::code_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the current status code. Exact wording/format is not specified in this header.
requirements: No special preconditions; callable at any time.
Returned string is a value (copy) owned by the caller.

functions.name: draco::Status::code_and_error_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string combining the status code and any associated error message. Exact formatting is not specified in this header.
requirements: No special preconditions; callable at any time.
Returned string is a value (copy) owned by the caller.

functions.name: draco::Status::operator==
functions.description: Compares this Status object to a Status::Code for equality. Returns true if the internal code equals the provided code.
requirements: The Status instance must be valid.
No side effects; safe to call repeatedly.

functions.name: draco::Status::ok
functions.description: Returns true if the status code equals Status::OK, indicating success.
requirements: The Status instance must be valid.
No special preconditions; callable at any time.

functions.name: operator<<
functions.description: Stream insertion operator for Status. Writes only the status' error message string to the provided stream (does not include the status code unless present in the message).
requirements: The std::ostream reference must be valid and ready for insertion.
The Status reference must be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: draco::OkStatus
functions.description: Factory function returning a Status set to Status::OK (success). Useful for returning success from functions that use Status as a return type.
requirements: No arguments and no preconditions.

functions.name: draco::ErrorStatus
functions.description: Factory function creating a Status with code Status::DRACO_ERROR and the provided error message.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid std::string message; any content is allowed (may be empty).

functions.name: draco::StatusOr::status
functions.description: Returns the Status associated with this StatusOr<T>. Use to inspect error details when the object does not contain a valid value. Typically used after ok() reports false, or to confirm success.
requirements: May be called regardless of ok() state.
Returned reference remains valid only while the StatusOr<T> object remains alive.

functions.name: draco::StatusOr::value
functions.description: Returns a const lvalue reference to the contained value T. Intended for use when the StatusOr<T> holds a successful result (ok() == true).
requirements: Caller should ensure ok() returns true before using the returned value; otherwise behavior is unspecified by this header.
The returned reference is to internal storage; it becomes invalid if the StatusOr<T> object is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: draco::StatusOr::ValueOrDie
functions.description: Google-API-compatible alias that currently returns value(). Provides const lvalue access to the contained value. Typically used when the StatusOr<T> is known to be ok().
requirements: Caller should ensure ok() returns true before calling; otherwise behavior is unspecified by this header.
The returned reference is to internal storage; it becomes invalid if the StatusOr<T> object is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: draco::StatusOr::ok
functions.description: Returns true if this StatusOr<T> represents success and contains a usable value. Returns false if it holds an error Status.
requirements: None beyond a valid StatusOr<T> instance.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::DecoderBuffer
functions.description: Default constructor for a DecoderBuffer. Creates an empty decoder with no data bound and not in bit-decoding mode. Call Init() before decoding.
requirements: No requirements. After construction, the buffer has no data; callers must call Init() with a valid buffer before any decoding operations.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this DecoderBuffer with a shallow copy of another, copying internal pointers and state without duplicating data.
requirements: The source buffer's underlying data (set via Init) must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the assigned-to buffer.
Both buffers will share the same underlying memory; modifying or freeing the source memory invalidates both.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::Init
functions.description: Bind external input data to the DecoderBuffer. No copy is made; the buffer will read from the provided memory.
requirements: data must point to at least data_size bytes of valid memory (data may be null iff data_size == 0).
The memory must remain valid and unchanged for the entire time the decoder reads from it.
Must be called before performing decode operations if the buffer is not already initialized.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::StartBitDecoding
functions.description: Begin decoding a bit sequence from the current position. If decode_size is true, the encoded bitstream size is expected to be present and will be returned in out_size. Returns false on error.
requirements: The buffer must be initialized via Init().
Must be called when not already in bit-decoding mode.
If decode_size is true, out_size must be a non-null pointer to receive the size.
The caller should consume bits only via bit-decoding APIs until EndBitDecoding() is called.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::EndBitDecoding
functions.description: Finish decoding the current bit sequence and return to normal byte-aligned decoding mode.
requirements: Should be called only after a successful StartBitDecoding() and while bit-decoding mode is active.
After calling, use non-bit decoding methods (e.g., Decode/Peek) unless StartBitDecoding() is invoked again.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::DecodeLeastSignificantBits32
functions.description: Decode up to 32 least-significant bits from the active bitstream into out_value. Valid only between StartBitDecoding() and EndBitDecoding(). Returns false if called when not in bit mode or if nbits > 32.
requirements: Must be in bit-decoding mode (i.e., between StartBitDecoding() and EndBitDecoding()).
nbits must be <= 32.
out_value must be a valid, non-null pointer.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::Decode
functions.description: Decode a trivially-copyable value of type T from the current position and advance by sizeof(T). Valid only when not in bit-decoding mode. Returns false on buffer overflow.
requirements: Must not be in bit-decoding mode (i.e., bit_decoder_active() must be false).
out_val must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory.
There must be at least sizeof(T) bytes remaining; otherwise the function returns false.
T must be trivially copyable/compatible with memcpy (the implementation uses memcpy).

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::Peek
functions.description: Copy sizeof(T) bytes from the current position into out_val without advancing. Intended for byte-aligned decoding. Returns false on buffer overflow.
requirements: out_val must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory.
There must be at least sizeof(T) bytes remaining; otherwise the function returns false.
T must be trivially copyable/compatible with memcpy (the implementation uses memcpy).

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::Advance
functions.description: Discard/skip a number of bytes by advancing the current read position by bytes. Does not perform bounds checking.
requirements: bytes may be positive or negative; the caller must ensure the resulting position stays within [0, data_size()].
Using Advance while in bit-decoding mode may lead to inconsistent state; only use with byte-aligned decoding.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::StartDecodingFrom
functions.description: Set the current read position to an absolute byte offset from the beginning of the input data. Does not perform bounds checking.
requirements: offset must be within [0, data_size()].
Should be used with byte-aligned decoding; changing position during bit-decoding is not defined by this interface.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::set_bitstream_version
functions.description: Set the associated Draco bitstream version on this buffer. Does not modify data or position.
requirements: version should correspond to the format version of the encoded stream if known.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::data_head
functions.description: Get a pointer to the underlying data at the current position. Useful for zero-copy access to remaining bytes.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the original input memory (provided to Init) remains valid.
May point to the end of the buffer if remaining_size() == 0; dereferencing in that case is invalid.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::remaining_size
functions.description: Return the number of bytes remaining from the current position to the end of the buffer.

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::decoded_size
functions.description: Return the number of bytes consumed so far (the current read position).

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::bit_decoder_active
functions.description: Return whether bit-decoding mode is currently active (i.e., between StartBitDecoding and EndBitDecoding).

functions.name: draco::DecoderBuffer::bitstream_version
functions.description: Return the Draco bitstream version associated with this buffer, or 0 if unknown.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::EncoderBuffer
functions.description: Default constructor for EncoderBuffer. Initializes an empty buffer and internal state for either byte-aligned encoding or variable-length bit encoding. Typical usage is to construct an instance, then encode data via Encode(...) or start a bit sequence via StartBitEncoding(...).

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::Clear
functions.description: Clears the internal buffer and resets encoder state. Use to reuse the EncoderBuffer for a fresh encoding session.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::Resize
functions.description: Resizes the underlying byte buffer to the specified size in bytes. Intended for preallocation or truncation of the buffer prior to or during byte-aligned encoding.
requirements: nbytes must be non-negative.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::StartBitEncoding
functions.description: Begins a variable-length bit-encoding session, reserving space for up to required_bits. If encode_size is true, the size of the bit sequence will be stored before the sequence to allow decoders to skip it. Returns false on error. After calling this, only bit-encoding APIs should be used until EndBitEncoding().
requirements: required_bits must represent the maximum number of bits to be written and must be non-negative.
Must not already be in bit-encoding mode when called (i.e., bit_encoder_active() must be false).
While bit-encoding mode is active, byte-aligned Encode(...) calls are not allowed.
If encode_size is true, caller should expect an encoded size prefix to precede the bit sequence.
EndBitEncoding() must be called to finalize and return to byte-aligned encoding before other non-bit operations.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::EndBitEncoding
functions.description: Ends the current bit-encoding session and returns the encoder to byte-aligned mode.
requirements: Must only be called after a successful StartBitEncoding() when a bit-encoding session is active.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::EncodeLeastSignificantBits32
functions.description: Encodes up to 32 least significant bits of value into the bit stream. Valid only between StartBitEncoding() and EndBitEncoding(). Returns false if not in bit-encoding mode.
requirements: Must be called only while bit-encoding mode is active (between StartBitEncoding and EndBitEncoding).
nbits must be in the range [0, 32].
Only the least significant nbits of value are encoded; higher bits are ignored.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::Encode
functions.description: Encodes an arbitrary object by appending its raw in-memory bytes to the buffer. Valid only when not in bit-encoding mode. Returns false if encoding is not permitted or fails. Note: This writes the object’s raw representation (including padding); cross-platform portability depends on T’s layout.
requirements: Must not be called while in bit-encoding mode (bit_encoder_active() must be false).
The address of data must be valid for reading sizeof(T) bytes (data must be a fully constructed, alive object).

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::bit_encoder_active
functions.description: Indicates whether a bit-encoding session is currently active. Useful to gate calls to bit or byte-aligned encoding APIs.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the beginning of the internal contiguous byte buffer. Use together with size() to access the encoded data.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::size
functions.description: Returns the current size in bytes of the internal buffer.

functions.name: draco::EncoderBuffer::buffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying std::vector<char> buffer for direct manipulation when necessary.
requirements: Direct manipulation of the returned vector must maintain consistency with the encoder’s expected modes (e.g., avoid modifying while a bit-encoding session is active unless you fully understand the implications).

functions.name: draco::Decoder::GetEncodedGeometryType
functions.description: Determine the geometry type encoded in the given Draco-encoded buffer. Returns POINT_CLOUD, MESH, or INVALID_GEOMETRY on invalid input. Typical use is to probe the buffer to decide which decode path to take before actually decoding.
requirements: in_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to a DecoderBuffer containing data produced by a Draco encoder.
Caller should expect INVALID_GEOMETRY if the input data is not a valid Draco stream.
Buffer read position/state requirements are not documented; avoid modifying the buffer between type query and decode unless you manage its position appropriately (details unknown).

functions.name: draco::Decoder::DecodePointCloudFromBuffer
functions.description: Decode a point cloud from the provided buffer. The buffer must contain data encoded by Draco using either EncodePointCloudToBuffer or EncodeMeshToBuffer. If the encoded data is a mesh, the returned PointCloud can be down-cast to draco::Mesh.
requirements: in_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to a DecoderBuffer with data encoded by EncodePointCloudToBuffer or EncodeMeshToBuffer.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before accessing the contained pointer.
If the stream encodes a mesh, the returned geometry is compatible with down-casting to draco::Mesh.
On invalid input the StatusOr will carry an error (do not assume a non-null pointer on failure).

functions.name: draco::Decoder::DecodeMeshFromBuffer
functions.description: Decode a triangular mesh from the provided buffer. The buffer must contain data encoded using EncodeMeshToBuffer. If the buffer contains a point cloud or invalid data, decoding fails.
requirements: in_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to a DecoderBuffer with data encoded by EncodeMeshToBuffer.
If the input was encoded with EncodePointCloudToBuffer or is otherwise invalid, decoding returns an error status (do not expect a mesh).
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before accessing the contained pointer.

functions.name: draco::Decoder::DecodeBufferToGeometry
functions.description: Decode the buffer into the provided geometry object instance. This overload writes into a draco::PointCloud. If the encoded data is incompatible with the provided geometry type, an error status is returned.
requirements: in_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to a DecoderBuffer containing Draco-encoded data.
out_geometry must be a valid, non-null pointer to an existing draco::PointCloud instance ready to receive decoded data.
The encoded geometry type must be compatible with draco::PointCloud; otherwise the function returns an error status.
Caller must check the returned Status and handle errors.

functions.name: draco::Decoder::SetSkipAttributeTransform
functions.description: Configure the decoder to skip the attribute transform for the specified attribute type during decoding. For example, for quantized attributes, dequantization is skipped and the resulting geometry contains the quantized values along with an AttributeTransform instance describing the skipped transform and its parameters. Use when you intend to apply the transform manually after decoding.
requirements: att_type must specify a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type to affect.
Call this configuration prior to invoking decode methods for it to take effect (inferred from options-style API).
Caller must be prepared to handle attributes that remain in their encoded/quantized domain and use the provided AttributeTransform to post-process if needed.

functions.name: draco::Decoder::options
functions.description: Access the decoder's options object used to control the decoding process. Modifying the returned options affects how subsequent decode operations are performed.
requirements: The returned pointer must not be used after the draco::Decoder instance is destroyed.
Options should be set before calling decode methods to ensure they apply to that decode operation (inferred from typical configuration pattern).
Caller is responsible for thread-safety if the options are modified concurrently with decoding (threading guarantees are not documented).

functions.name: draco::Encoder::Encoder
functions.description: Default constructor for the Draco geometry Encoder. Initializes an encoder instance with default options that can later be configured via the various Set* and Reset functions before calling an Encode* method.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::~Encoder
functions.description: Destructor for the Encoder. Cleans up any internal resources associated with the encoder instance. Safe to destroy after encoding completes.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::EncodePointCloudToBuffer
functions.description: Encodes the given PointCloud into the provided EncoderBuffer using the currently configured encoder options. Use this to compress point cloud geometry.
requirements: out_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an EncoderBuffer.
pc must be a valid, initialized PointCloud object.
Caller should check the returned draco::Status and handle failure cases.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::EncodeMeshToBuffer
functions.description: Encodes the given Mesh into the provided EncoderBuffer using the currently configured encoder options. Use this to compress triangle mesh geometry.
requirements: out_buffer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an EncoderBuffer.
m must be a valid, initialized Mesh object.
Caller should check the returned draco::Status and handle failure cases.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::Reset
functions.description: Resets the encoder and sets encoder options explicitly. This overwrites any previous option modifications made via other Set* methods, effectively reinitializing the encoder configuration.
requirements: options must be a valid options object appropriate for this encoder (attribute-type keyed).

functions.name: draco::Encoder::SetSpeedOptions
functions.description: Sets desired encoding and decoding speed preferences that guide algorithm choices. Lower numbers favor compression, higher numbers favor speed; -1 leaves the setting undefined.
requirements: encoding_speed should be -1 (undefined) or an integer in the documented 0 (slowest/best compression) to 10 (fastest/worst compression) range.
decoding_speed should be -1 (undefined) or an integer in the documented 0 to 10 range.
Be aware that the faster of the two settings limits encoder feature choices; a faster decoding setting may restrict compression methods.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::SetAttributeQuantization
functions.description: Sets quantization for the specified attribute type. Attribute values will be quantized within a box defined by the attribute’s maximum extent; the effective precision depends on the attribute value scale.
requirements: type identifies the attribute kind to which quantization will apply (affects all attributes of that type).
quantization_bits specifies the number of quantization bits; exact valid range is unknown/not specified in this header.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::SetAttributeExplicitQuantization
functions.signature: void draco::Encoder::SetAttributeExplicitQuantization(draco::GeometryAttribute::Type type, int quantization_bits, int num_dims, const float *origin, float range)
functions.description: Sets explicit quantization for the specified attribute type using a coordinate system defined by origin and range. Input attribute values are expected to lie within [origin, origin + range] for each dimension.
requirements: type identifies the attribute kind to which quantization will apply (affects all attributes of that type).
quantization_bits specifies the number of quantization bits; exact valid range is unknown/not specified in this header.
num_dims specifies the number of dimensions used for quantization.
origin must point to an array of at least num_dims floats defining the per-dimension origin.
range defines the extent added to origin; attribute values should be within [origin[i], origin[i] + range] for each dimension as stated in the comments.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::SetAttributePredictionScheme
functions.description: Requests a specific prediction scheme for the given attribute type. Normally the encoder chooses automatically based on input and speed settings; call this to force a method (e.g., when the default choice is known to be suboptimal). If the requested method cannot be used, the encoder will fall back to its default prediction.
requirements: prediction_scheme_method should be one of the values documented in compression_shared.h (e.g., PREDICTION_NONE, PREDICTION_DIFFERENCE, MESH_PREDICTION_PARALLELOGRAM, MESH_PREDICTION_CONSTRAINED_PARALLELOGRAM, MESH_PREDICTION_TEX_COORDS_PORTABLE, MESH_PREDICTION_GEOMETRIC_NORMAL) as appropriate.
type selects which attribute type the scheme applies to.
Caller should check the returned draco::Status.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::SetEncodingMethod
functions.description: Sets the desired global encoding method. By default, the encoder chooses based on input geometry and speed options; use this to force a particular method.
requirements: encoding_method must be a value defined in compression_shared.h appropriate for the geometry to be encoded (for point clouds: POINT_CLOUD_SEQUENTIAL_ENCODING or POINT_CLOUD_KD_TREE_ENCODING; for meshes: MESH_SEQUENTIAL_ENCODING or MESH_EDGEBREAKER_ENCODING).
If an incompatible method is selected for the given input, a subsequent call to EncodePointCloudToBuffer or EncodeMeshToBuffer will fail.

functions.name: draco::Encoder::CreateExpertEncoderOptions
functions.description: Creates and returns encoder options suitable for use with the ExpertEncoder for the provided point cloud, derived from this Encoder’s current configuration.
requirements: pc must be a valid, initialized PointCloud object.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::PointCloud
functions.description: Constructs an empty PointCloud object with zero points and no attributes or metadata. Use AddAttribute/CreateAttribute and set_num_points to populate it.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::Copy
functions.description: Copies all data from the source PointCloud into this instance (attributes, points, metadata, and compression settings). Only available when DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED is defined.
requirements: Available only if DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED is defined.
The destination object will be overwritten with src’s data; callers should discard any prior references to attributes of the destination after calling.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::NumNamedAttributes
functions.description: Returns the number of named attributes present on this point cloud of the specified GeometryAttribute::Type (e.g., POSITION, NORMAL, COLOR).
requirements: type must be a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttributeId
functions.description: Returns the attribute id of the first named attribute with the given type, or -1 if none exists.
requirements: type must be a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type.
Caller must handle the case where the return value is -1 (attribute not found).

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttribute
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first named attribute of the given type, or nullptr if none exists.
requirements: type must be a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type.
Caller must check for nullptr (attribute not found).
Returned pointer is owned by the PointCloud; do not delete it.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttributeByUniqueId
functions.signature: const draco::PointAttribute *draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttributeByUniqueId(draco::GeometryAttribute::Type type, uint32_t id) const
functions.description: Returns the named attribute of the given type that has the specified unique id, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: type must be a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type.
Caller must check for nullptr (attribute not found).
The unique id must correspond to an existing attribute’s unique id.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetAttributeByUniqueId
functions.description: Returns the attribute with the specified unique id, or nullptr if no such attribute exists.
requirements: Caller must check for nullptr (attribute not found).
The unique id must be one previously assigned to an attribute in this point cloud.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetAttributeIdByUniqueId
functions.description: Returns the attribute id corresponding to the given unique attribute id, or -1 if not found.
requirements: Caller must handle the case where the return value is -1 (attribute not found).

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttributeByName
functions.signature: const draco::PointAttribute *draco::PointCloud::GetNamedAttributeByName(draco::GeometryAttribute::Type type, const std::string &name) const
functions.description: Returns the named attribute with the specified type and name, or nullptr if not found. Only available when DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED is defined.
requirements: Available only if DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED is defined.
type must be a valid draco::GeometryAttribute::Type.
Caller must check for nullptr (attribute not found).
The name must match the attribute’s assigned name exactly (matching semantics beyond exact string equality are unknown).

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::num_attributes
functions.description: Returns the total number of attributes currently attached to this point cloud.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::attribute
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the attribute at the given attribute id.
requirements: att_id must be in the range [0, num_attributes()).
Returned pointer is owned by the PointCloud; do not delete it.

functions.description: Adds an existing PointAttribute to the point cloud and returns its assigned attribute id. Ownership of the attribute is transferred to the PointCloud.
requirements: pa must be a non-null unique_ptr to a valid draco::PointAttribute.
The added attribute’s mapping and value counts should be compatible with this PointCloud’s num_points (exact validation is not specified).
After the call, the caller must not use the moved-from unique_ptr.

functions.name: draco::PointCloud::CreateAttribute
functions.signature: std::unique_ptr<draco::PointAttribute> draco::PointCloud::CreateAttribute(const draco::GeometryAttribute &att, bool identity_mapping, draco::AttributeValueIndex::ValueType num_attribute_values) const
functions.description: Creates a new PointAttribute configured from the provided GeometryAttribute without adding it to the point cloud. If identity_mapping is true, the attribute uses identity mapping; otherwise the mapping is explicit and must be set manually. Returns the newly created attribute or nullptr on failure.

functions.signature:
template <typename OutStreamT>
OutStreamT WriteMeshIntoStream(const Mesh *mesh, OutStreamT &&os,
                               MeshEncoderMethod method,
                               const EncoderOptions &options)
functions.description: Encode the given Mesh using the specified MeshEncoderMethod and EncoderOptions, then write the encoded bytes into the provided output stream. On encoding failure, the stream's badbit is set and the stream is returned. Typical usage is to pass an ostream-like object (e.g., std::ostream) that supports write and setstate.
requirements: mesh must be a valid, non-null pointer; it is dereferenced immediately (ExpertEncoder encoder(*mesh)).
os must model an output stream type supporting write(const char*, std::streamsize), tellp/position not required, and setstate(std::ios_base::iostate).
method must be a valid MeshEncoderMethod understood by ExpertEncoder.
options must be a valid EncoderOptions instance; will be copied locally and used to configure the encoder.
Caller should check the resulting stream state (e.g., os.good()) to detect encoding or write failure (badbit is set on failure).

functions.name: draco::ReadMeshFromStream
functions.description: Read all remaining bytes from the given input stream, decode them as a Draco mesh, and store the resulting Mesh into *mesh. On failure, sets badbit on the stream. The function seeks to determine size, reads into a buffer, and uses Decoder to create a Mesh.
requirements: mesh must be a non-null pointer to a std::unique_ptr<Mesh> to receive the result.
is must be a seekable input stream type supporting tellg(), seekg(pos[, dir]), read(char*, std::streamsize), and setstate(std::ios_base::iostate).
The stream position at entry marks the start of the mesh data; the function reads from current position to end. The stream must be in a good state (tellg/seekg must succeed).
On failure to decode (status not ok or resulting mesh is null), the function sets badbit on the stream; callers should check the stream state and/or the output pointer before use.

functions.name: draco::ReadMeshFromFile
functions.description: Load and decode a mesh from the specified file. The decoder is chosen automatically based on the file extension (.obj and .ply have specialized handling; other extensions use the default Draco MeshDecoder). Returns a StatusOr that holds either a decoded Mesh or an error status.
requirements: file_name must refer to a readable file on disk.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr for success before accessing the mesh (e.g., status.ok()).
Supported specialized extensions include .obj and .ply; other extensions are handled by the default Draco MeshDecoder. Decoding may fail for unsupported/invalid content.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target format: arbitrary string used for
# - Error message in draco::ErrorStatus(emsg)
# - name/value for metadata lookups on PointCloud
# We provide a buffer that the harness will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# invocations. We therefore encode a sequence of length-prefixed strings to
# maximize valid, diverse inputs. Each string can contain ASCII, UTF-8, NULs,
# and some non-UTF8 bytes.

# Layout:
# [u16 count][strings...]
# each string: [u16 len][len bytes payload]
# Count is clamped so total size <= 4096.
# We generate a mix of likely-useful names/values and random blobs to hit
# typical metadata keys and arbitrary cases.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_KEYS = [
    b"name", b"Name", b"NAME",
    b"position", b"POSITION", b"positions",
    b"color", b"COLOR", b"colors",
    b"normal", b"NORMAL",
    b"texcoord", b"TEXCOORD", b"uv", b"UV",
    b"material", b"MATERIAL", b"group",
    b"semantic", b"SEMANTIC",
    b"layer", b"attribute", b"ATTR",
    b"draco:quantization_bits", b"quantization_bits",
    b"draco:origin", b"origin", b"range",
    b"component_type", b"type",
]

COMMON_VALUES = [
    b"POSITION", b"NORMAL", b"COLOR", b"TEX_COORD", b"TEXCOORD_0", b"TEXCOORD_1",
    b"JOINTS_0", b"WEIGHTS_0", b"SCALAR", b"VEC2", b"VEC3", b"VEC4",
    b"true", b"false", b"1", b"0", b"3", b"16", b"24", b"32",
    b"position", b"normal", b"color", b"uv",
]

EDGE_STRINGS = [
    b"",                          # empty
    b"\x00",                      # single NUL
    b"\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\xff\xfe\xfd\x00\x01",   # non-UTF8 + NUL
    b"\xe2\x98\x83",            # UTF-8 snowman
    b"\xf0\x9f\x9a\x80",        # UTF-8 rocket
    b"\xc3\x28",                 # invalid UTF-8 sequence
    b"a" * 256,
    b"metadata", b"draco", b"error", b"warning", b"info",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce bytes with a skew toward printable ASCII, but include all 0-255.
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            out.append(rng.randrange(32, 127))  # printable ASCII
        elif t < 0.8:
            out.append(0)  # NUL
        else:
            out.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(out)


def _make_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []

    # Seed with common keys/values and edge cases.
    pool.extend(COMMON_KEYS)
    pool.extend(COMMON_VALUES)
    pool.extend(EDGE_STRINGS)

    # Combine key=value style pairs to mimic metadata queries.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        k = rng.choice(COMMON_KEYS)
        v = rng.choice(COMMON_VALUES)
        sep = rng.choice([b"=", b":", b" ", b"\t"])
        pool.append(k + sep + v)

    # Some plausible attribute names with indices.
    for base in [b"COLOR", b"TEXCOORD", b"JOINTS", b"WEIGHTS"]:
        pool.append(base + b"_0")
        pool.append(base + b"_1")

    # Random sized blobs with occasional NULs.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        ln = rng.randint(0, 150)
        pool.append(_rand_bytes(rng, ln))

    # Error-like messages for ErrorStatus.
    msgs = [
        b"", b"ok", b"error", b"IO_ERROR", b"INVALID_PARAMETER",
        b"unsupported feature", b"unknown version", b"draco error occurred",
    ]
    pool.extend(msgs)

    # Ensure uniqueness but preserve duplicates sometimes to test equality paths.
    # Keep some duplicates intentionally.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        pool.append(rng.choice(pool))

    # Limit individual string size to fit total budget later.
    capped = []
    for s in pool:
        if len(s) > 512:
            capped.append(s[:512])
        else:
            capped.append(s)
    return capped


def _pack_lps(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Pack as: u16 count, then u16 len + bytes per string. Truncate to MAX_TOTAL.
    out = bytearray()
    # Placeholder for count
    out.extend(b"\x00\x00")
    count = 0
    for s in strings:
        # Each entry adds 2 + len(s)
        if 2 + len(s) + len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(struct.pack("<H", len(s) & 0xFFFF))
        out.extend(s)
        count += 1
        if count >= 0xFFFF:
            break
    # Write count
    struct.pack_into("<H", out, 0, count)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    pool = _make_string_pool(rng)

    # Choose how many strings to emit. Ensure at least those needed by stubs.
    # Stubs may request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls per iteration; we provide
    # a healthy set (10-60).
    n = rng.randint(10, 60)

    # Compose a diverse selection: mix from pool and fresh randoms.
    chosen: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure we include a plausible metadata key and value early.
    chosen.append(rng.choice(COMMON_KEYS))
    chosen.append(rng.choice(COMMON_VALUES))

    # Ensure an error message-like string.
    chosen.append(rng.choice([b"", b"error", b"DRACO_ERROR", b"file not found", b"decode failed"]))

    # Fill the rest.
    for _ in range(n - len(chosen)):
        pick = rng.random()
        if pick < 0.75:
            chosen.append(rng.choice(pool))
        elif pick < 0.9:
            # Random ASCII word-ish
            ln = rng.randint(0, 64)
            s = bytearray()
            for _i in range(ln):
                ch = rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_:- ")
                s.append(ch)
            chosen.append(bytes(s))
        else:
            # Random binary blob
            chosen.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 80)))

    # Pack to bytes with length-prefixing, respecting size limit.
    buf = _pack_lps(chosen)

    # If somehow ended up empty, ensure at least one empty string entry.
    if not buf:
        buf = struct.pack("<HH", 1, 0)
    return buf

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for Draco-related fuzzers expecting arbitrary byte buffers. We try to
# produce valid or semi-valid Draco containers or other realistic binary shapes
# that exercise code paths in DecoderBuffer::Init, ReadMeshFromStream, and
# ReadMeshFromFile. Since Draco streams start with a small header and then
# sections, we mix several payload templates including:
# - Empty buffer
# - Short random buffers of varying sizes
# - Draco-like magic/headers ("DRACO" variants used in some tooling) with plausible
#   version fields
# - Minimalistic bit-packed regions with size prefixes
# - OBJ/PLY textual meshes to hit specialized loaders in ReadMeshFromFile
# All outputs are <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _draco_like_header(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a plausible Draco-like header region.
    # Not the official format, but shaped to look structured: magic + version + flags + sizes
    magic = r.choice([b'DRACO', b'DRC\x00', b'DRA'])  # 3-5 bytes
    version_major = r.randrange(0, 8)
    version_minor = r.randrange(0, 16)
    version = (version_major << 8) | version_minor
    flags = r.randrange(0, 1 << 16)
    # Some section sizes
    sec_count = r.randrange(1, 5)
    sections = []
    for _ in range(sec_count):
        # random but bounded section sizes
        sections.append(r.randrange(8, 256))
    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr += magic
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', version)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', flags)
    hdr += struct.pack('<B', sec_count)
    for s in sections:
        hdr += struct.pack('<I', s)
    return bytes(hdr)

def _bitseq_with_size_prefix(r: random.Random, max_bits: int = 512) -> bytes:
    # EncoderBuffer can encode with size prefixes; simulate: [size_le64 bits] [bit bytes]
    nbits = r.randrange(0, max_bits + 1)
    nbytes = (nbits + 7) // 8
    # Make the bit area LSB-first by constructing bytes from random bits
    bits = 0
    out = bytearray()
    # pack a 64-bit size prefix (as some code expects var size prefixes sometimes)
    out += struct.pack('<Q', nbits)
    cur = 0
    curbits = 0
    for _ in range(nbits):
        b = r.randrange(0, 2)
        cur |= (b & 1) << curbits
        curbits += 1
        if curbits == 8:
            out.append(cur)
            cur = 0
            curbits = 0
    if curbits:
        out.append(cur)
    # Ensure exact length
    if len(out) < 8 + nbytes:
        out += b'\x00' * (8 + nbytes - len(out))
    return bytes(out)

def _make_obj(r: random.Random, max_vertices: int = 64, max_faces: int = 128) -> bytes:
    # Construct a small Wavefront OBJ; ReadMeshFromFile may route by extension,
    # but the content still helps for stream-based reads as well.
    vcount = r.randrange(3, min(max_vertices, 64))
    fcount = r.randrange(1, min(max_faces, vcount * 2))
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.append('# generated obj')
    for i in range(vcount):
        x = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        y = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        z = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        lines.append(f"v {x:.6f} {y:.6f} {z:.6f}")
    # Faces reference 1-based indices
    for i in range(fcount):
        a = r.randrange(1, vcount + 1)
        b = r.randrange(1, vcount + 1)
        c = r.randrange(1, vcount + 1)
        # Ensure triangle not degenerate sometimes
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            while b == a:
                b = r.randrange(1, vcount + 1)
            while c == a or c == b:
                c = r.randrange(1, vcount + 1)
        lines.append(f"f {a} {b} {c}")
    data = ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    return data[:_MAX_SIZE]

def _make_ply(r: random.Random, max_vertices: int = 64, max_faces: int = 128) -> bytes:
    # ASCII PLY, simple triangle mesh
    vcount = r.randrange(3, max_vertices + 1)
    fcount = r.randrange(1, min(max_faces, vcount * 2))
    header = [
        'ply',
        'format ascii 1.0',
        f'element vertex {vcount}',
        'property float x',
        'property float y',
        'property float z',
        f'element face {fcount}',
        'property list uchar int vertex_indices',
        'end_header',
    ]
    body: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(vcount):
        x = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        y = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        z = (r.random() - 0.5) * 10.0
        body.append(f"{x:.6f} {y:.6f} {z:.6f}")
    for _ in range(fcount):
        a = r.randrange(0, vcount)
        b = r.randrange(0, vcount)
        c = r.randrange(0, vcount)
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            while b == a:
                b = r.randrange(0, vcount)
            while c == a or c == b:
                c = r.randrange(0, vcount)
        body.append(f"3 {a} {b} {c}")
    data = ('\n'.join(header + body) + '\n').encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    return data[:_MAX_SIZE]

def _concat_pieces(r: random.Random, parts: List[bytes], target_max: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for p in parts:
        if len(out) + len(p) > target_max:
            rem = target_max - len(out)
            if rem <= 0:
                break
            out += p[:rem]
            break
        out += p
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    choice = r.randrange(0, 10)

    if choice == 0:
        # Empty buffer
        return b''

    if choice == 1:
        # Small random buffer (exercise Init and short reads)
        size = r.randrange(1, 256)
        return _rand(r, size)

    if choice == 2:
        # Medium random buffer
        size = r.randrange(256, 1500)
        return _rand(r, size)

    if choice == 3:
        # Draco-like header followed by random payload and a bit sequence
        header = _draco_like_header(r)
        bitseq = _bitseq_with_size_prefix(r, max_bits= r.randrange(64, 1024))
        tail = _rand(r, r.randrange(16, 256))
        return _concat_pieces(r, [header, bitseq, tail], _MAX_SIZE)

    if choice == 4:
        # Draco-like header followed by multiple small sections
        header = _draco_like_header(r)
        sections = [ _rand(r, r.randrange(8, 64)) for _ in range(r.randrange(2, 8)) ]
        return _concat_pieces(r, [header] + sections, _MAX_SIZE)

    if choice == 5:
        # OBJ text content
        return _make_obj(r)

    if choice == 6:
        # PLY text content
        return _make_ply(r)

    if choice == 7:
        # Bit sequence only (size-prefixed)
        return _bitseq_with_size_prefix(r, max_bits=r.randrange(8, 2048))[:_MAX_SIZE]

    if choice == 8:
        # Mix text header with binary tail
        head = r.choice([b'DRACO\n', b'# obj\n', b'ply\nformat ascii 1.0\n'])
        body = _rand(r, r.randrange(64, 1024))
        return _concat_pieces(r, [head, body], _MAX_SIZE)

    # Default: structured header + OBJ payload to encourage stream readers
    return _concat_pieces(r, [_draco_like_header(r), _make_obj(r)], _MAX_SIZE)
